description: We are Team Krushang from Pune, India. Led by Krushang (9 yrs) with parent support. Our mission: Create a Junior Astronaut Training Story about ISS - Abandoned but Not Forgotten. We focus on Best Use of Storytelling Award. We use NASA open data to teach kids about mission trade-offs through story, art & simple game concept. Skills: Storytelling, Research, Presentation.d
summary:
Our project is a handwritten storybook by Krushang, age 9 from Pune, India. It tells the emotional story of rovers left behind on Mars and Moon.

Many kids think rovers left on Mars are trash. Our book says NO - they are heroes left on purpose!

We feature Spirit who found proof of water, Opportunity who ran a 45km marathon and sent 217,000 photos, Curiosity who used a sky-crane landing and still explores finding ancient lakes, plus Moon heroes Lunokhod (Russia 1970) and Vikram (India's South Pole).

Using NASA open data for accuracy, we personify rovers with feelings to make science fun for children. Our message: "Batteries may sleep but discoveries live forever."

It addresses the NASA challenge "Who Lives on Mars? No One - But Our Robots" by showing robots are our family there, waiting to say hello when humans arrive. It inspires kids to love space, not fear it.
details:
What does it do: Our project is a 6-page handwritten storybook "We Are Not Trash, We Are Heroes!" by Krushang (9, Pune). It changes kids thinking from "rovers are trash left on Mars" to "rovers are heroes left on purpose".

How it works: We researched using NASA Open Data (Mars Exploration Program, Moon missions). We picked 5 heroes: Spirit (found water proof), Opportunity (217k photos, 45km marathon), Curiosity (sky-crane landing, still active), Lunokhod 1 (Russia 1970 Moon), Vikram (India). We gave them emotions and dialogues to make kids connect.

Benefits: Makes space science emotional and fun for age 5-12. Teaches to respect space heritage. Uses simple language, hand drawings, real facts.

Impact: Kids will love space, not fear. They will understand humans leave robots as family on Mars to wait for us. Inspires future ISRO/NASA scientists from India.

Tools: Handwritten book (paper, colors), Canva for text overlays, VN Video Editor for 30sec demo, Google Drive, NASA Open Data Portal, images from NASA JPL.

Creativity: Rovers talk! "I am not sleeping trash, I am taking rest after work". 9-year-old perspective. Mix of Indian (Vikram, Chandrayaan) + Global heroes. Message: Batteries may sleep but discoveries live forever.

Team considered: Use accurate NASA facts, keep language child-friendly, show both Mars and Moon, include India, keep video under 30 sec, all links public.
